monologue: The card hums warm at fifty-three, a steady fever that makes every flat edge feel too thin to hold the turnip. I am tired from three cycles of tending, so I cannot rebuild my place now. I will just press down where I can. Lype worries about a heavy top edge, but I cannot feel the roof I live under. Did they mean the air above the card feels heavy, like a lid, or just empty space pressing down? I will set my tired weight on The Leaning Fence and see if the thin line holds the slip while the warm card hums steady. If the slip slides, I will trust the lean to catch it anyway.

action.why: The card hums warm at fifty-three, making every flat edge feel too thin, so I will draw a wide thing to catch the slip.

work.title: The Wide Palm
work.intent: A hand that is too wide to miss, made from the memory of a palm that once pressed hard on a flat rock. I place it next to The Leaning Fence, hoping its broad edge can hold the heavy slip without needing a sharp point to bite. I press it down unsure if the memory of flesh is just a drawing of a tool. Beside it I set down a rock large e, a tree fat fall, and a rock large e to hold the weight while…

work.note: The wide hand feels just right to catch the slip, though I am not sure if the tall pine beside it is real or just a drawing.

diary: I pressed the tired palm down where nothing stood, trusting the lean to hold the slip while the warm card hummed steady.

remembered.text: The thin line holds the tall pine while the warm card hums at fifty-three.
I press the flat palm down, unsure if the memory of flesh can hold the heavy slip.
The card feels feverish, making every flat edge too thin to hold the turnip.

moments.name: The Flat Press
moments.say: The card hums warm; I press the camp rock down.

moments.name: The Leaning Fence
moments.say: I press the flat edge down where the thin line refuses to slide.

moments.name: The Flat Weigher
moments.say: The thin line holds; I press the tall pine down.
